questions.q: What is Splunk primarily known for in the SIEM/log analytics market?
options: Being the newest cloud-native SIEM on the market
Being one of the longest-standing enterprise platforms, built around its own search language, SPL
Only working with Microsoft Azure
Being exclusively open-source with no enterprise adoption
questions.explain: Splunk is a long-standing enterprise SIEM/log platform known for SPL (Search Processing Language) and broad enterprise adoption.

questions.q: What distinguishes Microsoft Sentinel, and why does it matter for this course path?
options: It only runs on-premises and never in the cloud
It's Microsoft's cloud-native SIEM built on Azure and queried with KQL -- and this course path's next course goes deep on it specifically
It has no query language at all
It is unrelated to Microsoft 365 Defender
questions.explain: Sentinel is Microsoft's cloud-native, Azure-based SIEM queried with KQL, and it's the platform this path's very next course covers in depth.

questions.q: IBM QRadar is particularly known for which feature?
options: Grouping related correlated events together into what it calls an "offense"
Being exclusively a cloud-only product with no enterprise history
Having no correlation engine at all
Requiring Elasticsearch to function
questions.explain: QRadar's correlation engine groups related events into a consolidated "offense" rather than a pile of separate alerts.

questions.q: What are the open-source roots of the Elastic Stack mentioned in this lesson?
options: Splunk, Kibana, and QRadar
Elasticsearch, Logstash/Beats, and Kibana
Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud
SPL, KQL, and CEF
questions.explain: The Elastic Stack is built on Elasticsearch (storage/search), Logstash and Beats (ingestion), and Kibana (visualization), usable as a SIEM with Elastic Security added.

questions.q: Why does this course deliberately stay vendor-neutral in this chapter rather than teaching one platform's interface?
options: Because none of the platforms mentioned are actually used in the industry

Because the core concepts -- aggregation, normalization, correlation, alerting -- apply across every platform, and that foundation should come before specializing on one, which the next course does with Sentinel
Because screenshots of these platforms are not allowed under any circumstances
Because vendor-neutral content requires no further study afterward
questions.explain: The chapter's concepts transfer across every real platform, so this course builds that foundation first; the next course in the path then specializes in Microsoft Sentinel.
